To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
dogs with CE harbor more mucosal bacteria than controls and that dogs with intestinal neoplasm have more adherent and invading mucosal bacteria than dogs with CE.
dogs with chronic enteropathies had an increased mucosal microbiota, which was associated with disease severity and pathogenic events.
dogs with chronic enteropathies have more bacteria adhered to their intestinal epithelium and that this may contribute to their disease.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the intestinal microbiota in chronic enteropathies of dogs.
the study of the intestinal mucosa of dogs and the microbiota that inhabits it.
understanding how the mucosal microbiota is altered in CE, and how the microbiota may be involved in the pathogenesis of these disorders.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the ileal and/or colonic mucosal bacterial communities in dogs with CE are characterized by increased numbers of mucosa-adherent and/or invasive mucosa-associated bacteria compared to controls.
in dogs with chronic enteropathies, there is an increased number of mucosal bacteria, which is associated with clinical disease activity.

in canine CE, there is a shift in the composition of the ileal mucosal microbiota, with an increase in the numbers of Clostridium coccoides/E. rectale group and Bacteroidales bacteria, and a shift in the spatial organization of the colonic mucosal bacterial community.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ileal and colon mucosal microbiota is altered in dogs with IBD, GC, and intestinal neoplasias.
the ileal and colon mucosal microbiota of healthy dogs and CE dogs is predominantly colonized in a spatial manner.
the canine mucosal microbiota is a dynamic entity that is influenced by disease and may be a target for therapeutic intervention.
The main takeaway from our work is that
mucosal microbiota are altered in dogs with CE, and that these alterations are different for each disease.
dogs with CE, regardless of the disease type, harbor increased numbers of mucosal bacteria belonging mainly to the Clostridia, Bacteroidetes, and Proteobacteria phyla.
CE dogs harbor increased mucosal bacteria belonging mainly to the Clostridia-coccoides group, Bacteriodes, Enterobacteraceae, and E. coli.
